rationale: The question is whether the package works in usual classes with usual instructors, which is a pragmatic effectiveness question. Individual allocation by a central office keeps classes intact, attendance comes from existing registers, and reminders with missed-week calls have raised attendance elsewhere (c1), while falls cannot be powered (c3). Peer calls may add home exercise (c2). PRECIS-2 domains are set near the pragmatic end.
alternatives: Allocation by centre (refused: 14 centres give too few clusters and centres differ in transport and population)
Before-after comparison of the 2026 and 2027 intakes (refused: attendance varies by season and instructor)
whyNotMoreComplex: A factorial design separating reminders from peer calls would need about four times the sample; the programme's decision is about the package.

decision.statement: Run a pragmatic trial with individual allocation by a central office in all 14 centres, comparing usual classes with classes plus the adherence support package, with attendance at two thirds of sessions as the primary outcome.
decision.question: Should the programme test the adherence support package in a pragmatic trial in 2027?

criteria.text: Reminders and missed-week calls raised attendance elsewhere, peer calls were linked to more home exercise, and falls cannot be powered, so attendance is the right primary outcome.
Fewer than eight trained peer volunteers are available when the first intake starts.

gates.requirement: Programme manager approval for the package and central allocation
gates.evidence: Approval FPM-2027-03 dated 2026-09-12, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval of the trial

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from the two retrieved records; none of the five model leads is cited. The ethics gate is unknown, so the action stays blocked.

summary: Pragmatic trial recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims from two retrieved records and waits for ethics approval.
